question: Find the difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years at 10% p.a. on a sum of Rs. 400.
solution:
**Given:**

Sum = Rs 400

Rate of interest = 10% p.a.

Time = 2 years

**Concept Used:**

Simple Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100

Compound Interest = Principal (1 + r/100)t – Principal

**Calculation:**

⇒ Simple Interest = (400× 10× 2)/(100) = Rs 80

⇒ Compound Interest = 400(1+(10)/(100))² – 400

⇒ Compound Interest = 400 × (11)/(10)× (11)/(10) – 400 = 484 – 400 = Rs 84

⇒ Difference between SI and CI = 84 – 80 = Rs 4

**Therefore, the difference between compound interest and simple interest is Rs 4.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

**Concept used:**

Difference between C.I & S.I for 2 years = P × [R/100]2

**Calculation: **Difference between C.I & S.I for 2 years = 400 × [10/100]²

Difference between C.I & S.I for 2 years = Rs. 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**
